issues: Meaning drift in heading: "SALINANBUPATI PROBOLINGGO" rendered as "COPY REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO"; should be "COPY" (Salinan) and "REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO" (Bupati Probolinggo) as separate elements, not implying the regent is a copy.
Minor meaning drift/terminology: "Menimbang" more properly rendered as "Whereas" (recitals) rather than "Considering" in this legal context (to align with Indonesian legal drafting).

Broken heading structure: original has 8 top-level (#) headings at the start; translation adds an extra top-level heading "# COPY" and shifts the rest, so headings no longer match one-to-one in order.

Meaning drift in heading: "SALINANBUPATI PROBOLINGGO" is rendered as separate headings "COPY" and "REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO"; it should be a single heading equivalent to "COPY OF THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO" to match the original structure. (Also "Negera" should be "State" but translation already uses correct meaning.)

Scrambled/merged list markers: several list items are run together (e.g., Article 1 items 2–3; Article 3 letter e; Article 5 letters e–f and g–h; Article 7(3) letters a and d; Article 10 letter e), which breaks downstream list boundary detection.
Minor meaning drift/terminology: 'Dinas' is translated as 'Agency' inconsistently; better as 'Office/Service (Dinas)' to reflect a government department.

Scrambled/merged list markers: several items run together (e.g., Article 13 'and/or  d.', Article 15 'and/orc.', Article 16 'andg.', Article 17 'ande.', Article 21 'andc.', Article 22 'by:a.' and later '...; g.' on same line, Article 23 'activities:a.' and 'and/org.', Article 24 multiple 'through:a.' / 'andc.' / 'include:a.' / 'andb.'), which breaks downstream boundary detection.

Meaning drift/typo: Article 19(3) should be 'further regulated by a Regent Regulation' (Peraturan Bupati), not 'Regent Regulation' as a type name is fine but should include the article 'a' to match normative phrasing; otherwise meaning is same.
Markdown/list structure not faithfully preserved as separate list items due to missing line breaks before certain markers (a., b., c., d., g., etc.).

Scrambled/altered list formatting: several list items in the original run together (e.g., Article 13 c–d; Article 14 a–c; Article 15 b–c; Article 16 f–g; Article 17 d–e; Article 21 b–c; Article 22(1) c–h; Article 23(1) f–g; Article 23(2) f–g; Article 24(1) b–c; Article 24(2) b–c; Article 24(3) a–b; Article 24(4) a–b). Translation introduces extra blank lines and inconsistent marker placement; needs normalization to ensure each marker appears once in correct order with its content.
Meaning drift/awkward rendering: Article 17(a) mistranslates 'penghormatan dan penggunaan sepenuhnya' (should be 'respect for and full enjoyment/exercise of rights', not 'full use').

Scrambled/merged list structure: several lettered items are run together with preceding text (e.g., 'to:a.', 'h...; i.', 'ando.', 'youth;d.', 'andj.', 'andf.', 'andb.', 'andd.'), which breaks marker boundaries required for downstream splitting.
Numbering structure issue: Article 30 paragraph (4) is merged into paragraph (3) instead of being a separate '(4)' item.

Minor meaning drift/terminology: 'Bagian' is translated as 'Part' (acceptable), but several merged markers risk changing which content belongs to which item; corrected by restoring exact item boundaries per the Indonesian source.
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 41: item h is merged into item g on the same line; item k is merged into item j ("and/ork.") and the marker "k." is not properly separated.

Scrambled/merged numbering and sub-items in Article 43: paragraph (2) is merged into paragraph (1) after item c; sub-items under (2) are merged ("a. reprimand; orb. written warning") and missing proper separation.
Scrambled/merged numbering in Article 44: paragraph (3) is merged into item k on the same line instead of being a separate numbered paragraph.
Scrambled/incorrect list numbering in Article 43: item (2) in the original is merged into item 1 and the marker "(2)" is missing; list markers must appear once and in the same order.

Meaning drift in Article 45(2): original refers to "paragraph (1) and paragraph (2)" (even though (2) does not exist in the article); translation should preserve this reference exactly rather than correcting it to (1) and (2) based on context.

Minor meaning drift/typo carryover in Article 41(j)-(k): original has a formatting error where "dan/atau" runs into "k."; translation should reflect two separate items j and k (already done) but ensure j ends with a semicolon and k ends with a period to match list structure.
